environment: Optimized macOS ARM64 native host and Rust schema 22 server, disposable stock Zaton
setup: The private relay supplied the same 200 stationary grounded poses in a compact grid near one Zaton encounter in both runs. Each measurement began after all 200 native proxies became active.

stockSchedulerPolling.fixture: 200 synthetic grounded player poses delivered in each Rust heartbeat by the private relay

nativeFramePolling.fixture: 200 synthetic grounded player poses delivered in each Rust heartbeat by the private relay

analysis: The stock scheduler calculated a 265 ms A-Life interval. Reading the socket every frame recovered the 10 Hz roster cadence while the stock schedule continued to run A-Life.
scope: These were native proxies and real Rust processes with synthetic pose input. Real WebRTC clients, separated activation sites, WAN and longer population testing are separate gates. The relay queue drop count includes startup and proxy creation.
initialHarnessFailure: The first 200-proxy run aborted on a Unix socket ENOBUFS. The repeated test counted that condition and let the next full snapshot repair it, as the production sender does.
